dossier.public_summary: The claimed dip changes dramatically from sector to sector and only a few unusually deep transits create the signal. A real planet's dips should repeat at the same depth, so this looks like stellar variability or noise-corrupted measurements rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies by >400% across sectors (118 to 1201 ppm) with chi2 219.6 for 7 dof, inconsistent with a stable planet.
Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent; three outliers (1958, 2262, 909 ppm) carry most of the signal, not a repeatable small dip.
No strong V shape or odd/even/secondary, but shape alone does not override direct depth instability evidence for variability/systematics.
